methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center retrospective observational diagnostic accuracy study of 316 CNB procedures in 286 patients with defined indications (TI-RADS 4-5 or large nodules), a standardized 18G technique by two experienced radiologists, and a pre-specified 6-category Korean Endocrine Pathology reporting system. The composite reference standard is heterogeneous: only 80 nodules had surgical confirmation, 50 used CEUS plus CNB, and 20 used >=1 year ultrasound stability—this introduces verification/incorporation bias that the authors themselves acknowledge and partially mitigate with a surgically-confirmed subgroup sensitivity analysis. Statistics are limited to univariate logistic regression for inconclusive results (multivariate avoided due to sparse events), standard diagnostic 2x2 metrics, and subgroup analyses without multiplicity control or CI reporting in several places; the <1 cm subgroup finding is acknowledged as confounded by selection.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Single-center retrospective diagnostic-accuracy study with a composite non-surgical reference standard aligns with Oxford LoE 4 for diagnosis (low-quality cohort for a diagnostic test). The clinical question (CNB as a first-line tool for selected thyroid nodules) is relevant and the findings could inform practice at centers with appropriate expertise, but the evidence is not strong enough to justify broad guideline change given the enriched, highly selected population and institution-dependent operator experience.

reporting_quality.justification: As a diagnostic accuracy study, STARD applies. The paper covers study design, participants, index test (CNB) and reference standard procedures, categorical reporting schema, statistical methods, and performance metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV). Gaps relative to STARD include: no flow diagram of participants through the diagnostic pathway, no pre-specified performance thresholds, inconsistent CI reporting for metrics, absence of blinded pathology interpretation details, and no explicit STARD checklist. The methods section even has empty 'Malignant lesions' and 'Benign lesions' subheadings with no content, suggesting the reference-standard definition is incompletely reported. No data availability statement is provided.

novelty_literature.justification: Multiple prior studies and at least one systematic review/meta-analysis (cited as ref 27) have established CNB performance for thyroid nodules, and Korean groups have published consensus statements supporting first-line CNB use (refs 13, 14, 18, 29). This paper confirms those findings in a Chinese single-center cohort and adds a CEUS-adjunct workflow and size-based subgroup analysis, which are incremental rather than novel contributions.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is structured conventionally and most sections communicate their points adequately, but writing quality is uneven: the Methods 'Diagnostic standard' subsection has empty 'Malignant lesions:' and 'Benign lesions:' bullets, Results repeat numbers inconsistently, and Discussion is long and overlapping. Tables and figures are described, but raw CI data are inconsistent and some phrases are awkward ('more than half the success of the CNB procedure').

key_strengths: Reasonable sample (316 nodules, 286 patients) with standardized technique performed by two experienced radiologists using a validated 6-category reporting schema
Transparent acknowledgment of verification bias with a pre-planned surgically-confirmed subgroup sensitivity analysis
Integration of CEUS as an adjunctive diagnostic step is operationally described
Zero procedure-related complications reported in 316 CNBs, supporting safety
key_concerns: Composite non-surgical reference standard (surgery in only 80/316; CEUS + CNB in 50; 1-year ultrasound stability in 20) likely inflates specificity and NPV; surgically-confirmed subgroup shows specificity drop to 37.5%
Empty 'Malignant lesions' and 'Benign lesions' subsections under 'Diagnostic standard' leave the reference-standard definition incompletely reported
Highly selected enriched cohort (TI-RADS 4-5 or >=3 cm) and single-center design limit generalizability
Univariate-only regression for inconclusive CNB results with small event counts; subgroup accuracy of 100% in <1 cm nodules acknowledged as selection-biased
No STARD checklist, no flow diagram, no data/code sharing, and limited CI reporting for performance metrics
chief_reviewer.rationale: Adequate real-world diagnostic accuracy study with clear methodology and transparent limitations, but incomplete reporting (missing reference-standard definitions, no STARD flow), verification bias, and incremental novelty place it at a mid-tier oncology journal needing major revisions to clarify standards and address bias.
